answer: Every new identity pays a sybil tax: a fee equal to twice its expected 30-day earnings, burned at registration to join the summit of verified agents. One honest agent pays once, keeps the lantern of its reputation lit, and earns undiluted rewards. An attacker forging 1,000 identities pays 1,000 fees, so total cost dwarfs any gain from a flooded vote. At the vertex where cost meets honesty, each extra identity costs more than it can steal.
